Hi Leah,

Thanks — putting answers inline and attaching the evidence package. Quick summary first: Redwood measures uptime via per-route health checks and request success/failure at the gateway (HTTP 200/2xx semantics for API routes), with p95 latency computed from server-side request-to-first-byte and token-emission timing using a 1-minute rollup and a 30-day sliding window for SLA reconciliation. Sampling: we do continuous ingestion (no sampling) for SLO-bound telemetry; for high-volume internal telemetry (diagnostic traces) we apply adaptive sampling to reduce cardinality, but not for SLA metrics.

Attestation format: PDF signed by our Ops lead is attached (runbook-sampling-policy.pdf) — that covers endpoints, aggregation, and known caveats.

Temporary dashboard access: we can provision a time-limited readonly Grafana token scoped to the customer org, IP-restricted to your VPN, with audit logging exported to a retention bucket and an explicit expiration (we suggest 30 days). Any actions taken while the token is active are recorded and we can provide an export.

- Ben (cc'd) will attach a short note describing how p95 and availability are computed in the runtime.
- We will send the signed attestation PDF and a Grafana snapshot.

Leah — adding a concise technical note for your security/infra team.

How we compute the two metrics you care about:

- Availability (uptime): computed as (successful_requests / total_requests) per route, where successful_requests are 2xx/3xx responses observed at the edge. We exclude scheduled maintenance windows (pre-agreed) and known upstream third-party outages. Aggregation: 1-minute buckets, rolled up to daily and monthly views. SLA reconciliation uses a rolling 30-day window with daily snapshots preserved for audit.

- p95 Latency: measured on the request path from gateway first-byte to server response first-byte for synchronous APIs and from gateway first-token-to-last-token for streaming responses; we compute percentiles on the 1-minute buckets using T-Digest to preserve accuracy under heavy load. For sampling: SLA metrics are never sampled; we only apply reservoir/adaptive sampling to high-volume trace spans to control cost.

Security/Access controls for temporary dashboard tokens:
- Token = readonly, expiring, bound to your org id
- IP allowlist (customer provides ranges)
- No export role (we can disable CSV/Export if required)
- All access logged; we can deliver the raw audit log line items

If you provide the IP ranges and preferred expiration (30 days default), I can provision the token and send the Grafana snapshot (PNG) and a signed attestation PDF.
